suggestions: FINDINGS.md Data section says 'normalised in prep.py; 45 challenges total' -- 45 is the PRE-alias-merge name count; post-normalisation there are 40 challenges (verified). As written, the sentence misleads; reword to '45 raw names -> 40 challenges'.

Synthetic recovery was run at sigma_c = 1.8 (Q1 shape) / 2.5 (crossed, joint), but the real fits land at sigma_c ~ 4.9 (joint) and 4.9-9.1 (per-model). The HalfNormal(2) prior on sigma_challenge has ~1.4% mass above 4.9, so some unquantified downward shrinkage of sigma_c (and latent ICC) in the real crossed/joint fits is plausible. The prior-sensitivity caveat partially covers this and the headline quantities are observed-scale, but a recovery replicate at sigma_c ~ 5-6 would close the loop on finding 1's '4.9-9.1 logits' claim.

Curve B's k=10 annotation (SE 0.0075) excludes the run-effect floor (+/-2.7 accuracy points) established in finding 5; a reader of the plot alone could conclude sub-1% benchmark SE is achievable. Add the run floor as a horizontal reference line or a note on the plot/finding 3.
'mostly one o3-mini batch' for the Helm failures: 2,360/2,814 rows are o3-mini but spread across ~10 runs of 280 rows; 'batch' is loose (trivial wording).

State explicitly in FINDINGS that no within-run duplicate (run, item, epoch) rows exist (the check was effectively done via the run-level hash, and I verified 0 in raw, but the brief asks for it and it deserves one line).
summary: Exceptionally solid work. Every quantitative claim in FINDINGS.md traced to an output file or independently recomputed from the posteriors/raw parquet with zero discrepancies beyond rounding. Data archaeology (39% re-ingestion duplicates, mechanistically-diagnosed degenerate runs, item_id normalisation) is exactly what this warehouse needed and is itself a finding. Validation exceeds the brief: design-matched synthetic recovery with an honestly-disclosed 27/28, plus frequentist MC and MCMC cross-checks of the design curve. Convergence exceptions are confined to provably non-identified nuisance directions with correct written justification. Remaining suggestions are wording fixes and one genuine (non-blocking) gap: synthetic recovery was not exercised at the extreme sigma_c regime the real data occupies, so the latent-scale spread numbers rest partly on the stated prior-sensitivity caveat.
